newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New Zealand proposes future pension saving scheme.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand proposes future pension saving scheme.

text.p: New Zealand on Monday launched a long-awaited and controversial contributory pension scheme which, if introduced, would require all earners who can to save about NZ$120,000 ($81,000) towards the cost of their pension.

A government white paper published during the day said that if a referendum due in September endorses the Retirement Savings Scheme (RSS), everyone earning over $96 a week would have to contribute 3.0 percent of their incomes from July 1998.
The exact level of the annuity towards which the payments must go will be set after consultation with the fund management industry which is expected to offer personal schemes, it added.

The required contribution level will rise over the five years following introduction to 8.0 percent, provided the government can afford the tax cuts it has promised would be brought in to offset the increased contributions.
The 86-page document said the compensatory tax cuts would be guaranteed in the first year, but thereafter would only happen "when fiscally sustainable".
Under a plan intended to avoid any distortion between men and women's contributions, the paper proposes giving women extra to match the men's annuity level.
